worked.title: Q1 · Eigenvalues, diagonalisation, singular values (8 marks)

problem.text: A = [[3, 1, 0], [1, 3, 0], [0, 0, 4]]. (a) All eigenvalues and eigenvectors. [5M] (b) Diagonal D and invertible P with AP = PD. [2M] (c) Singular values of the given upper-triangular B, where BᵀB = A. [1M]

steps.label: (c)
steps.text: BᵀB = A, so the singular values of B are √(eigenvalues of A) = **√2, 2, 2** [1M].

worked.priorityWhy: Recent paper: sit it as a timed mock (≈ 3.4 min per mark)

worked.title: Q2 · Independence, subspace, basis, rank, determinant (8 marks)

problem.text: v₁ = (−3, 1, 0, −1), v₂ = (0, 2, 3, 4), v₃ = (0, 1, 0, 0), v₄ = (−6, 3, −3, −3). (a) Dependent or independent? [3M] (b) Prove U = span{v₁, …, v₄} is a subspace; basis and dimension. [3M] (c) Rank and determinant of B = [v₁ v₂ v₃ v₄]. [2M]

steps.label: (a) Matrix
steps.text: Put the vectors as columns of B [1M].

steps.label: (a) Echelon form
steps.text: R1 ↔ R2; R2 + 3R1; R4 + R1; then eliminate below the second and third pivots ⇒ rows (1, 2, 1, 3), (0, 6, 3, 3), (0, 0, −3/2, −9/2), (0, 0, 0, 3) [1M].

steps.label: (a) Conclude
steps.text: Every column has a pivot, so v₁, …, v₄ are **linearly independent** [1M].

steps.label: (b) Subspace
steps.text: u = Σaᵢvᵢ and w = Σbᵢvᵢ give u + w = Σ(aᵢ + bᵢ)vᵢ ∈ U [1M]; cu = Σ(caᵢ)vᵢ ∈ U [1M]. (Only stating "closed under both" gets 1M, not 2.)

steps.label: (b) Basis
steps.text: Independent and spanning ⇒ {v₁, v₂, v₃, v₄} is a basis; **dim U = 4** [0.5M + 0.5M].

steps.label: (c)
steps.text: Four non-zero rows ⇒ **rank 4** [1M]. det B = (−1)(row swap) × 1 × 6 × (−3/2) × 3 = **27** [1M].

worked.answer: Independent; U is a subspace with basis {v₁, …, v₄}, dim 4; rank 4, det 27.
worked.priorityWhy: Recent paper: sit it as a timed mock (≈ 3.4 min per mark)

worked.title: Q3 · Inner product, constrained problem, dual and KKT (8 marks)

problem.text: A = [[3, 1], [1, 3]], ⟨u, v⟩ = uᵀAv. Cost C(x, y) = 2‖(x, y)‖² in this norm; region R: x + y − 1 ≥ 0, x + y − 3 ≤ 0. (a) Properties A needs, proved. [2M] (b) Formulate the problem. [1M] (c) Lagrangian and dual. [2M] (d) Verify KKT at (x, y, λ₁, λ₂) = (½, ½, 8, 0). [3M]

steps.label: (a)
steps.text: A must be symmetric and positive definite [0.5M]. A = Aᵀ [0.5M]. Leading minors 3 > 0 and 9 − 1 = 8 > 0 ⇒ positive definite [1M].

steps.label: (b)
steps.text: ‖X‖² = XᵀAX = 3x² + 2xy + 3y² ⇒ **min 6x² + 4xy + 6y²** s.t. x + y ≥ 1, x + y ≤ 3 [1M].

steps.label: (c)
steps.text: g₁ = 1 − x − y ≤ 0, g₂ = x + y − 3 ≤ 0. L = 6x² + 4xy + 6y² + λ₁(1 − x − y) + λ₂(x + y − 3) [1M]. Dual: max D(λ₁, λ₂) = min over x, y of L, s.t. λ₁, λ₂ ≥ 0 [1M].

worked.answer: A symmetric PD; min 6x² + 4xy + 6y² on 1 ≤ x + y ≤ 3; all four KKT conditions hold at (½, ½, 8, 0).
worked.priorityWhy: Recent paper: sit it as a timed mock (≈ 3.4 min per mark)

worked.title: Q4 · Least-squares loss, convexity, GD with inverse decay (8 marks)

problem.text: Data (x, y): (5, 3), (6, 5); ŷ = w₀ + w₁x; J = ½Σ(ŷᵢ − yᵢ)². (a) J explicitly, its Hessian, and prove J convex. [3M] (b) ∇J. [1M] (c) From (0, 0), two GD iterations with ηₜ = η₀/(1 + kt), η₀ = 0.1, k = 0.4, t = 1, 2. [4M]

steps.label: (a) Convex
steps.text: 2 > 0 and det H = 122 − 121 = 1 > 0 ⇒ H positive definite ⇒ J convex [2M].

worked.priorityWhy: Recent paper: sit it as a timed mock (≈ 3.4 min per mark)

worked.title: Q5 · Hard-margin SVM: two separating lines (8 marks)

problem.text: X1 (2, 2) +1, X2 (4, 4) +1, X3 (2, 0) −1, X4 (4, 0) −1. (a) Hard-margin primal. [2M] (b) Show x₂ = 1 separates. [2M] (c) Show x₂ − x₁ = −1 separates. [2M] (d) Margin of each; which is better? [2M]

steps.label: (a)
steps.text: min ½(w₁² + w₂²) [1M] s.t. 2w₁ + 2w₂ + b ≥ 1, 4w₁ + 4w₂ + b ≥ 1, −(2w₁ + b) ≥ 1, −(4w₁ + b) ≥ 1 [1M].

steps.label: More
steps.text: Full write-up with the method: [Lecture 14, Hard margin tab](#/sem1/aiml-zc416/ch14/f-hard/1).

worked.answer: Both separate; margins 1 and 0.7071, so x₂ = 1 is better.
